checks: The declared complementary-cap formula applies to the two equal full-dimensional endpoints with their true midpoint M as the containing middle body. Its residual volume at the ordinary centroid of M is at most (1-Gamma)m. The two endpoint shifts are opposite and preserve the same affine margin average.

The endpoint-volume normalization divides by a and leaves the formula in r=m/a. From 4/11<Gamma<=1/2 and r<=11/8, the root x=[(1-Gamma)r]^(1/d) lies in [1/2,1), so 0<=2x-1<=x^2 gives the stated quadratic payment without changing signs.

The difference from Gamma(2-r) is concave in r. Exact endpoint values are Gamma(1-Gamma) and delta_d, with the latter smaller because the increasing difference polynomial is -9/4 at Gamma=1/2. The concave delta polynomial has minimum at least 55/7744 and maximum at most 55/256 on [4/11,1/2]. Hence c_d<2.

The integer hull grouping keeps exactly A,K,B: a nonzero endpoint group at base zero contributes a midpoint lying in M subset K. Every continuous-normal through-g_M cap adds at least Gamma m to the paired estimate, and every purely integer through-source halfspace pays k+a. At g_K its own cap alone pays Gamma k in every relevant direction.
The first normalized guarantee decreases in k/a and the second increases. The chosen branch is the larger one, with minimum at c_d/Gamma, giving Gamma c_d/(c_d+2Gamma)>Gamma/2.
Matched 8407bedf6b42ff39 §§1–3 and the exact surplus-window locators. The selected marks are the two stated true centroids, and the window is a condition on M's actual volume.

The frozen statement gives an explicit pointwise endpoint surplus and a deterministic switch between the ordinary centroids of M and K in the stated volume window.

The accepted two-cut result gives an existence guarantee throughout the equal-endpoint class at a different selected point and depends on middle and endpoint volumes. It does not give the displayed all-shift pair estimate or the stated two-mark rule.
Its scalar residual bound is used exactly at equal endpoint volumes and middle M. The new quadratic surplus and switching argument are subsequent conclusions.
